message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2024) | Area | Key Rights | What It Means for You | |------|------------|-----------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | Keep a copy of the lease, move‑in inspection report, and receipts for any repairs you paid for. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must keep the property in a **safe, sanitary, and livable condition** (plumbing, heating, electrical, etc.).
• Must comply with all local building and health codes. | If something is broken (e.g., no heat, leaky roof), you can request repairs. If the landlord fails, you may withhold rent or take legal action. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major issue within a reasonable time, you may **deduct the cost of repairs** from your rent (up to the amount of the rent). | Document the issue, send a written notice, and keep receipts. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter your unit without **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) except in emergencies. | If the landlord enters without notice, you can ask them to leave and may pursue damages. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For a **month‑to‑month lease**, the landlord must give **30 days’ notice** to terminate.
• For a fixed‑term lease, the landlord can only terminate for cause (e.g., non‑payment, violation of lease). | Keep track of lease terms and any notices you receive. | | **Rent Increases** | • Landlords can raise rent at the end of a lease term or with a 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month agreements. | Review the lease for any rent‑increase clauses. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on **race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or source of income** (e.g., public assistance). | If you suspect discrimination, you can file a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights. | | **Fair Housing** | • Landlords must comply with the **Fair Housing Act** and Texas Fair Housing laws. | This includes providing reasonable accommodations for disabilities. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must provide a **written notice** (e.g., 3‑day notice for non‑payment, 30‑day notice for lease termination).
• Eviction must go through the court; landlords cannot forcibly remove you. | If you receive a notice, respond promptly and consider legal counsel. | | **Lease Termination** | • You can terminate a lease early if the landlord breaches the lease or if the unit becomes uninhabitable. | Provide written notice and document the breach. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide essential utilities (water, heat, electricity) unless otherwise specified. | If utilities are cut off, you can demand restoration. | | **Maintenance Responsibilities** | • Tenants are responsible for keeping the unit clean and disposing of trash properly. | Keep records of any maintenance requests. | | **Subletting** | • Many leases allow subletting with landlord approval. | Obtain written permission before subletting. | | **Insurance** | • Landlords are not required to provide renter’s insurance, but it’s highly recommended. | Protects your personal property and liability. | #### Practical Steps to Protect Your Rights 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Understand all terms, including rent amount, security deposit limits, and notice periods. 2. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of all communications, receipts, and inspection reports. 3. **Use Written Notices** – Send any repair requests or lease termination notices in writing (email or certified mail). 4. **Know the Law** – Familiarize yourself with the Texas Property Code (especially Chapters 92–94) and local ordinances. 5. **Seek Legal Help** – If you face eviction, disputes over deposits, or discrimination, consult a tenant‑rights attorney or a local tenant advocacy group. --- **Quick Reference:** - **Security Deposit**: ≤ 1 month (unfurnished) or ≤ 2 months (furnished). - **Notice to Enter**: 24 hours (unless emergency). - **Notice to Terminate**: 30 days (month‑to‑month). - **Eviction**: Must go through court; no “self‑eviction.” If you have a specific situation (e.g., landlord refusing to repair, notice of eviction, or a dispute over a deposit), let me know and I can give more tailored advice.
